summary: Uma Chakravarti works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied at Miranda House (~1958–1962) and the University of Delhi (~1958–1964), where she completed her doctorate under D. Devahuti.

Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana works in Indology and related fields. He studied at Ayurveda College, Coimbatore (until 1992) and the University of Amsterdam (until 2000). He held posts at FRLHT (1995), Amala Institute, and the University of Toyama (1998, 2003–2004).

Unrai Wogihara (1869–1937) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Junjirō Takakusu and Ernst Leumann (~1899–1905) at the University of Strasbourg (~1899–1908). He later held posts at the University of Tokyo and Taisho University (~1926–1937).

Uranchimeg B. Ujeed is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. at SOAS University of London and served as a Research Associate in the Mongolia and Inner Asia Unit at the University of Cambridge.

Uranchimeg Tsultemin specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, earning a Ph.D. from UC Berkeley (~2004–2009). She has held posts at UC Berkeley, National University of Mongolia (2013–2014), Yonsei University, IUPUI (~2019), and the University of Iceland.

Urs App works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Gymnasium St. Antonius Appenzell, the University of Fribourg, and Temple University, training under Yoshitaka Iriya, Richard DeMartino, and Seizan Yanagida. He held posts at Hanazono University and EFEO.

Ute Hüsken is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies scholar. She completed her dissertation at the University of Göttingen (~1988–1995) under Heinz Bechert and held a post at Heidelberg University around 2017.

V. Raghavan (1908–1979) was an Indology scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Madras (1931–1934) under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served on the Madras faculty from ~1935 to 1973 and edited two scholarly journals.
Vaibhav Singh is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Reading in 2017 and held a post there attested in 2018.
Vajragupta is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He served as director of the Birmingham Buddhist Centre in 1997 and as Director of the Triratna Buddhist Community, attested in 2010.

Valdo H. Viglielmo (1926–2016) worked in Japanology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania and Harvard University (~1948–1956), later holding posts at Meiji Gakuin University (~1953–1955), Princeton University (~1960–1965), and the University of Hawaii (~1965–2002).
Valeria Gazizova works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her master's thesis at the University of Oslo under Per Kvaerne, attested in 2009.
Vasily Radlov (1837–1918) specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1854–1858) and held a post at Kunstkamera (~1894–1918).

Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi (1893–1985) was a scholar of Indology and history. He served as Principal and Professor of Sanskrit at Morris College (~1942–1947) and GVISH (~1947–1950), and later as Honorary Professor at Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University (~1957–1966).

Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale (1901–1991) was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and Sinologist who earned his PhD from the University of Bonn (-1930). He held posts at Fergusson College, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Delhi (attested 1966).

Vasudha Narayanan is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Madras, the University of Mumbai, and Harvard University (~1974–1978), and became Distinguished Professor of Religion at the University of Florida (~1982).
Verity Harte is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge (~1987–1994). She held academic posts at King's College London (~1997–2005) and Yale University (~2005).

Vesna A. Wallace specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. After earning her doctorate at UC Berkeley, she held posts at UC Berkeley, the University of Oxford (until 2010), and UC Santa Barbara (attested 2007–2014).
Victor B. Lieberman is a historian who studied at Yale University (~1963–1967) and SOAS University of London (~1970–1976). He joined the faculty at the University of Michigan around 1984.
Victor Chan is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Chicago. Around 2004, he served as Executive Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program at the University of British Columbia.
